instruction: Generate the No License / No IP Transfer provision for an employee confidentiality and invention assignment agreement between Cascade Digital Solutions Inc. (a Delaware corporation, the "Company") and Jordan Rafferty (a California individual, the "Employee"). Effective Date: March 18, 2025. Industry: large technology employer onboarding a senior engineer (confidentiality + invention assignment). Deal size: enterprise. Negotiation posture: provider-friendly. Confidentiality survival period: 5 years after termination. Governing law: California, with venue in Santa Clara County. Regulatory frameworks to address: California Labor Code Section 2870 (employee invention exemption), Defend Trade Secrets Act of 2016 whistleblower notice, California Business & Professions Code Section 16600 (post-employment non-compete ban). Specific requirements: Defend Trade Secrets Act whistleblower immunity notice in the required statutory form. Drafting style: BigLaw formal — long sentences, defined-term-heavy, WHEREAS recitals, formal third-person voice. Cover the standard provisions: no license granted by implication, estoppel, or otherwise, all rights reserved by the Disclosing Party, Disclosing Party retains all patent, copyright, trademark, and trade secret rights.
output:
ARTICLE 8 — NO LICENSE OR OWNERSHIP TRANSFER

8.1 Ownership Reserved. All Confidential Information and all Work Product shall be and remain the sole and exclusive property of the Company Group. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as granting Employee, by implication, estoppel, or otherwise, any license or other right under any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, or other intellectual property right of the Company Group, except such limited right to use Confidential Information as is necessary for Employee to perform the Purpose during the term of Employee's employment.

8.2 All Rights Reserved. The Company Group reserves all rights in and to its Confidential Information and Work Product, including without limitation all patent, copyright, trademark, and trade secret rights therein.

instruction: Write the Equitable Remedies section for a mutual non-disclosure agreement for a pharmaceutical licensing due diligence review between BlueShift Analytics Inc. (a Delaware corporation, the "Party A") and Avandra Biosciences, Inc. (a Delaware corporation, the "Party B"). Effective Date: February 24, 2025. Industry: pharmaceutical company licensing diligence on a Phase 2 oncology asset. Deal size: enterprise. Negotiation posture: balanced. Confidentiality survival period: 1 year after termination. Governing law: Delaware, with venue in New Castle County. Regulatory frameworks to address: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records), FDA pre-submission meeting materials confidentiality, HIPAA (to the extent patient-level data is disclosed). Specific requirements: clinical trial data room with watermarked CRF tables and pseudonymized patient-level data. Drafting style: BigLaw formal — long sentences, defined-term-heavy, WHEREAS recitals, formal third-person voice. Cover the standard provisions: acknowledgment that breach may cause irreparable harm, right to seek injunctive relief without posting bond, no obligation to prove actual damages, cumulative remedies in addition to any at law or in equity.
output:
ARTICLE 9 — EQUITABLE REMEDIES

9.1 Irreparable Harm. Each Party acknowledges that any breach of this Agreement may cause the Disclosing Party irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be inadequate, particularly with respect to clinical data, regulatory submissions, and manufacturing know-how.

9.2 Injunctive Relief. Each Party is entitled to seek specific performance, injunctive relief, and other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction, without posting bond and without proving actual damages, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity. Remedies are cumulative.

instruction: Generate the Term and Survival provision for a master non-disclosure agreement with per-deal confidentiality schedules between Riverstone Software Inc. (a Delaware corporation, the "Sponsor") and Liberty Pharmaceuticals Inc. (a Colorado corporation, the "Bidder"). Effective Date: August 5, 2024. Industry: private equity firm operating a shared data room with per-deal confidentiality schedules. Deal size: enterprise. Negotiation posture: balanced. Confidentiality survival period: 5 years after termination. Governing law: Colorado, with venue in Denver County. Regulatory frameworks to address: HSR Act antitrust pre-closing conduct, Securities Exchange Act anti-tipping rules. Specific requirements: shared data room access protocol with tiered access levels defined per Schedule. Drafting style: Modular MSA + Order Form — bare master agreement with all commercials pushed into a separate Order Form. Cover the standard provisions: term of the Agreement with end date or ongoing relationship, survival of confidentiality obligations for a defined period after termination, trade secret obligations survive as long as the information remains a trade secret, termination for material breach.
output:
ARTICLE 9 — TERM AND SURVIVAL

9.1 Term. This Master Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for a period of five (5) years thereafter, and shall automatically renew for successive one-year periods thereafter unless either Party provides sixty (60) days' prior written notice of non-renewal.

9.2 Survival. Notwithstanding any expiration or termination of this Master Agreement or any Confidentiality Schedule, the Receiving Party's obligations of confidentiality and non-use with respect to Confidential Information disclosed in connection with each Deal shall survive for the Survival Period specified in the applicable Confidentiality Schedule (or, if none is specified, for the default Survival Period of three (3) years from the conclusion of the Deal). With respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a Trade Secret, the obligations shall survive for so long as the information qualifies as a Trade Secret under applicable law.

9.3 Termination of a Specific Schedule. Either Party may terminate a specific Confidentiality Schedule on written notice to the other Party in the event of a material breach by the other Party that is not cured within sixty (60) days of written notice.

instruction: Generate the Confidentiality Obligations provision for a click-through beta program non-disclosure agreement between PrismLogic Software Solutions, Inc. Industry: developer tools vendor running a closed-beta API program. Deal size: smb. Negotiation posture: provider-friendly. Confidentiality survival period: 5 years after termination. Drafting style: Click-through Terms of Service — terse numbered lists, no preamble, no signature blocks, accept-by-clicking style. ARTICLE 3 — CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION

3.1 Participant will: (a) hold Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose; (c) disclose Confidential Information only to Participant's employees who have a need to know for the Purpose and who are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as these terms; and (d) protect Confidential Information using at least a reasonable degree of care.

instruction: Prepare the Compelled Disclosure article for a one-way confidentiality agreement for Canadian bank outsourcing due diligence between Apex Workflow Platform, Inc. (an Ontario corporation, the "Bank") and North Ridge Cloud Systems Ltd. (an Ontario Canadian corporation, the "Vendor"). Effective Date: February 28, 2024. Industry: Canadian Schedule I bank conducting cloud vendor outsourcing diligence under OSFI B-10. Deal size: enterprise. Negotiation posture: customer-friendly. Confidentiality survival period: 1 year after termination. Governing law: Ontario, with venue in Toronto. Regulatory frameworks to address: OSFI Guideline B-10 (Third-Party Risk Management), OSFI Guideline B-13 (Technology and Cyber Risk Management), Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA), Bank Act (Canada). Specific requirements: PIPEDA-compliant handling of any personal information disclosed during diligence. Drafting style: Customer paper / heavily negotiated — visible customer-side markups, audit rights, sub-processor lists, regulator pass-through. Cover the standard provisions: prompt written notice to the Disclosing Party before disclosure, cooperation with the Disclosing Party's efforts to obtain a protective order, disclosure limited to the portion legally required, continued confidentiality over non-disclosed portions.
output:
ARTICLE 5 — COMPELLED DISCLOSURE

5.1 Legal Process. In the event that Vendor or any of its Representatives is requested or required by any court, governmental authority, or other legal process to disclose any Confidential Information of the Bank, Vendor shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide the Bank with prompt prior written notice of such request or requirement so that the Bank may, at its sole cost, seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy or (at the Bank's sole election) waive compliance with this Agreement with respect to such disclosure.

5.2 Limitation on Compelled Disclosure. If a protective order is not obtained and the Bank does not waive compliance, Vendor may disclose only the minimum portion of Confidential Information that Vendor's outside legal counsel advises is legally required to be disclosed, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain assurances that confidential treatment will be accorded to such Confidential Information. Vendor shall continue to treat all non-disclosed portions as confidential.

5.3 Regulator Inquiries. For the avoidance of doubt, any inquiry or request from a Regulator directed at Vendor that relates to Confidential Information of the Bank is a "request or requirement" subject to this Article 5, and Vendor shall route any such inquiry through the Bank's compliance function before responding, to the extent legally permissible.

regulatory_frameworks: OSFI Guideline B-13 (Technology and Cyber Risk Management)
Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA)

ARTICLE 2 — PURPOSE

2.1 Narrow Purpose. Each Receiving Party shall use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information solely for the Purpose. instruction: Prepare the Confidentiality Obligations article for a mutual non-disclosure agreement for a potential acquisition transaction between Vertex Cloud Software, Inc. (a Delaware corporation, the "Party A") and Halcyon Specialty Chemicals LLC (a Delaware limited liability company, the "Party B"). Effective Date: April 22, 2025. Industry: strategic M&A due diligence (specialty chemicals acquisition). Deal size: enterprise. Negotiation posture: balanced. Confidentiality survival period: 3 years after termination. Governing law: Delaware, with venue in New Castle County. Regulatory frameworks to address: Securities Exchange Act Regulation FD, HSR Act antitrust pre-closing conduct, Delaware General Corporation Law fiduciary duties. Specific requirements: no residuals clause — memory of Confidential Information is NOT permitted use. Drafting style: BigLaw formal — long sentences, defined-term-heavy, WHEREAS recitals, formal third-person voice. Cover the standard provisions: definition of Confidential Information (marked, identified as confidential, or information a reasonable person would treat as confidential), use restriction — Confidential Information used solely for the defined Purpose, disclosure restriction — limited to personnel with a need to know who are bound by equivalent confidentiality, standard of care — at least the care the Receiving Party uses for its own confidential information, but no less than reasonable care, no transfer of IP or ownership to the Receiving Party, obligation to notify the Disclosing Party of any unauthorized disclosure.
output:
ARTICLE 3 — CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION

3.1 Obligations of the Receiving Party. The Receiving Party shall (a) hold the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in strict confidence, (b) use such Confidential Information solely for the Purpose in accordance with Article 2, (c) disclose such Confidential Information only to those Representatives who have a bona fide need to know such Confidential Information for the Purpose and who are bound by written or professional obligations of confidentiality and non-use no less protective than the obligations set forth in this Agreement, and (d) protect such Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care the Receiving Party uses to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature, but in no event less than a reasonable degree of care.

3.2 Responsibility for Representatives. The Receiving Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Agreement by any of its Representatives and shall take all reasonable measures (including without limitation, where appropriate, the institution of injunctive or other equitable proceedings) to restrain its Representatives from any unauthorized use or disclosure of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.

3.3 Notification of Unauthorized Disclosure. The Receiving Party shall promptly, and in any event within five (5) business days after discovery, notify the Disclosing Party in writing of any unauthorized use or disclosure of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information of which the Receiving Party becomes aware, and shall cooperate reasonably with the Disclosing Party in any effort by the Disclosing Party to mitigate or remedy such unauthorized use or disclosure.

3.4 Data Room Protocol. To the extent that either Disclosing Party makes Confidential Information available to the Receiving Party through a virtual data room, the Receiving Party shall comply with any data room access protocols designated by the Disclosing Party, including without limitation: (a) restrictions on printing, downloading, or copying of watermarked documents; (b) limitations on the number and identity of Representatives granted access; (c) maintenance of an access log upon request of the Disclosing Party; and (d) return or deletion of any locally retained copies upon conclusion of the review.
